sentences.text: Applicant is in detention since 01.09.2023.

2. Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed with liberty to revive the prayer after prosecutrix's evidence before the trial Court vide order dated 12.01.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.42272/2023.
3.

As per the prosecution story, on 19.08.2023, major prosecutrix aged 29 years filed an application in writing before police stating that her marriage was settled with present applicant on 15.10.2021 and solemnization of marriage was fixed for 17.10.2023.
In the meantime, on 16.10.2023, applicant established physical relations with her and thereafter repeatedly established physical relations with her.
The family members of the applicant started to demand Rs.8,00,000/- cash and marriage expenditure.
Her father was not in a position to pay that much amount.
Due to which now they have refused to perform marriage.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated only because marriage could not be performed.
It is further submitted that applicant never established physical relations with the prosecutrix.
All allegations are fabricated and forged.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Now there is no possibility of influencing of the prosecution witnesses and tempering with the prosecution evidence.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the victim have opposed grant of bail.
6. In this case, prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Now there is no possibility of influencing of the prosecution witnesses and tempering with the prosecution evidence.

Therefore, having taken into consideration the custody period of the applicant and other facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I a m inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant - Sanjay Singh Raghuwanshi be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
